proposal.text:
PROPOSAL for hugh (revises 7a2d2ea4 to make the short event-hash input form first-class, per hugh 2026-08-28): adopt the two design-gated gs-usability directions from review 4917b9da, which the cheap-wins request 1e9d35ab deliberately excludes because they touch the id-resolution and admission boundaries.

(A) ID RESOLUTION — accept what the orientation commands display. gs and the MCP should accept, for any event reference (rests_on, target, and the read verbs inspect/ratify/review), either a #N sequence index or an unambiguous event-hash prefix or suffix, and resolve it to the full canonical id (git:sha1:<genesis>#git:sha1:<event>) at the CLI/MCP boundary BEFORE signing, with the genesis and scheme defaulted from the workroom so a novice types exactly the short id the display shows. This is a resolution feature, not a format change, and it carries hard invariants:
 - Resolve at the tool boundary only; the SIGNED payload always stores the full 40-char canonical id, never a prefix. A prefix unique today can collide as the log grows, so a stored prefix is a time-bomb citation.
 - Scope the uniqueness scan to the durable EVENT set (the resident projection; the offline gs path scans refs/seq), not git's whole object database — a hex prefix could otherwise match an unrelated blob or tree.
 - Ambiguous or no-match input must REFUSE loudly, listing the candidates; never guess. This is distinct from, and must never be conflated with, the fold's 'a citation resolving to nothing is admitted in silence' contract, which governs SIGNED citations to absent events, not human input.
 - On writes (rests_on/target), echo the resolved full canonical id the act is about to sign, so a mis-resolution is caught before it becomes durable.
 The fold is unchanged: #N and short hashes mean nothing to the fold, which resolves only canonical ids (SKILL.md is explicit). Recommendation: adopt, resolve at the CLI boundary only.

(B) SUBMIT-TIME BASIS VALIDATION (unchanged from 7a2d2ea4): today gs state accepts --rests-on '#1' or a nonexistent id and the fold rules the act effective, because 'a citation resolving to nothing is admitted in silence' is a deliberate append-only contract. The novice-facing fix is to WARN at the CLI (not refuse in the fold) when a --rests-on value is malformed or resolves to nothing in the current projection, and to surface post-submit that the act rests on an unknown or dead basis — preserving the fold's silence-admits contract while stopping a novice from silently creating stale-from-birth work. Coordinate with the in-flight admission work (claude staleness-policy 769006ed refuseDeadBases split, codex completion-reliability ratify-preflight 4f3310a8) so the CLI warning and the write-boundary behaviour agree.

On ratification, planner files the implementation request; the cheap-wins lane 1e9d35ab proceeds independently and first. This proposal replaces 7a2d2ea4.
